format.title: Create a pack
format.intro: A pack is a JSON file that adds content on top of the base rules (SRD 5.2.1): species, backgrounds, subclasses, feats, spells, monsters and tools. It never replaces or removes any. Write it in a text editor, check it below, then import it from the <packs>Packs</packs> page.
format.structureIntro: <c>format</c> and <c>system</c> are written as is. <c>version</c> (1.0.0 by default), <c>author</c>, <c>language</c>, <c>translations</c> and <c>description</c> are optional, like each list of <c>content</c>. An unknown field gets the file refused: it is often a typo.
format.structureNote: author credits who wrote the pack — you, or the community member whose work you are reusing: it shows everywhere the pack appears. language gives the pack's language ("fr" or "en", French by default): a badge flags it to readers of another language. A file weighs 900 KB at most. Summarize the rules in your own words: don't copy a book's text.
format.rulesNote: « Field rules » downloads <c>ak-pack.schema.json</c>, a JSON Schema giving each field its type, accepted values, lengths and bounds — what the import checks. Give it to your text editor for autocompletion, or to an AI along with the example pack so it writes a valid pack. References between entries and unique ids are only checked by the checker, below.
format.ids: The pack and each of its entries have an <c>id</c> in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: <c>path-of-the-zealot</c>. Once loaded, the entry becomes <c>my-pack:path-of-the-zealot</c>: two packs can never collide, nor with the SRD. Each entry also has a <c>name</c>, shown as is.
format.refIntro: When an entry names another one (a background's origin feat, a spell):
format.refSame: an id defined in the same pack points to that entry;
format.refOther: a full id <c>other-pack:x</c> points to another pack, which must be loaded;
format.refSrd: otherwise, it is an SRD id: <c>alert</c>, <c>misty-step</c>…
format.refEnglish: Abilities, skills, classes, sizes, damage types… are written by their English id: each section lists the ones it accepts.
format.idName: Id and name, like every entry.
format.translationsIntro: One pack can be read in several languages. <c>language</c> says which language it is written in; <c>translations</c> gives, for each other language, its translated texts. Each reader sees the pack in their language when it has it, in the pack's otherwise.
format.translationsShape: A translation follows the shape of the entries, grouped by id, keeping only the texts: names, blurbs, summaries, labels. Lists follow the same order (<c>traits</c>, <c>features</c>, <c>attacks</c>, <c>choices</c>), lineages go by the option's name. A missing text stays in the pack's language.
format.translationsValues: Ids, numbers and values (<c>school</c>, <c>classes</c>, <c>damageKind</c>…) are not translated. Species options and spell variants keep their name on the sheet: their translation (<c>choice.options</c>, <c>spellVariants.options[].name</c>) is only used for display.
